use: What is the part used for? FUNCTIONAL: a working stand/support/enclosure/bracket/protective bumper. DECORATIVE: figurine/ornament only. PROTOTYPE: a temporary model for checking fit/shape. A beautiful working enclosure is FUNCTIONAL. Ignore appearance, load, environment and flexibility when deciding use. Bare force numbers or vague things have UNKNOWN use.
load: What LOAD MAGNITUDE is explicitly requested? LIGHT: weak/minimal/light load or explicitly no load. NORMAL: explicitly ordinary working load. HIGH: explicitly high/heavy load or heavy-duty strength requirement. UNKNOWN if unspecified. Force numbers alone do not establish severity. Impacts/vibration describe type, not magnitude. Normal thing, beautiful, fast, smooth do not describe a load.
loadKind: What MECHANICAL LOAD TYPE is explicitly stated? STATIC: constant mechanical force. IMPACT: hits/falls/shocks. CYCLIC: repeated mechanical loads/vibration. UNKNOWN if unspecified. Do not infer static just from a part name, and do not treat constantly outdoors as a force.
environment: What operating ENVIRONMENT is explicitly stated? INDOOR: home/room use. OUTDOOR: outdoors/rain/sun. HEAT: hot environment/operating temperature. UNKNOWN if unspecified. Electronics alone does not imply heat. Respect no heating/not outside. Prefer HEAT if heat and outdoor coexist.
flexibility: Does the part explicitly need to BEND? FLEXIBLE: soft/elastic/must bend or spring. RIGID: rigid/must not bend/not flexible. UNKNOWN if unspecified. A smooth/beautiful surface has nothing to do with flexibility. A load or a part name alone does not establish flexibility.
goal: What PRINT PRIORITY is explicitly stated? DETAIL: beautiful/smooth surface or fine detail. FIT: precision/dimensions/fit test. SPEED: fast/draft printing. ECONOMY: save filament/cost. UNKNOWN if unspecified. Just/simple/ordinary/do it well and a generic part name are NOT priorities. Do not infer speed from vague praise or surface quality from just a stand.
